finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and saves it. Any authenticated user can set privileged fields such as role, isAdmin, id, tenantId or ownerId, which allows privilege escalation or account/tenant takeover.
finding.source: req.body (JSON) from any authenticated user on PUT /me

trace.note: Object.assign merges all body keys into req.user
The updated user object is returned

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist or schema validation in this file. No field filtering before the save. The sibling route /me/profile destructures only displayName and bio, which shows the intended behaviour. Authentication middleware is not visible here, since it is presumably upstream and sets req.user, but it cannot restrict which fields are written. Object.assign with an own '__proto__' key from JSON.parse does not pollute the prototype, so the issue is limited to the user's own fields.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 does Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, then saves at users.js:6 and returns at users.js:7, so any authenticated user can write privileged fields (the sibling route at users.js:11-12 shows the intended allowlist); no other file in the directory defines guards, and the actual field names (role etc.) are not visible but the unrestricted write is.
